points.description: States that a queue is a data structure (or abstract data type / linear collection) that stores a collection of elements/items in order.

States the First In First Out (FIFO) principle: the element added first is removed/processed first (equivalent wording such as 'first come, first served' accepted). Do not accept LIFO or 'last in first out'.

levels.says: Mentions FIFO or ordering only vaguely (e.g. 'items are processed in order') without clearly stating first in is first out.

points.description: Names the enqueue operation: adding an element at the rear/back/end of the queue (accept 'add', 'insert', 'push' at the back).

levels.says: Names enqueue but does not say where/what it does, or describes adding at the back without naming it.

points.description: Names the dequeue operation: removing an element from the front/head of the queue (accept 'remove', 'delete', 'pop' from the front).

levels.says: Names dequeue but does not say where/what it does, or describes removing from the front without naming it.

rubric.notes: Full marks for: a data structure, FIFO, enqueue (add at rear) and dequeue (remove from front). The model answer earns all 5 marks. Part marks for vague or incomplete versions of FIFO or the operations; no marks for LIFO/stack descriptions.

selftest_notes: The model answer scored only 4 of 5.
